name_note: GTDB places this species in the genus Claveliimonas; the genomes and the papers cited here use the NCBI name Dorea ammoniilytica.

sentences.text: Dorea ammoniilytica was identified and characterized as a deoxycholic acid-producing species from two strains derived from human feces.
Those strains harboured segmented bai gene operons and showed high deoxycholic acid production activity from cholic acid in culture experiments.
The species was reported to belong to a distinct lineage from other known deoxycholic acid producers and from Dorea species.
The genus Claveliimonas was proposed for obligately anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive bacilli isolated from faecal samples of healthy Japanese people.
